name: Smoke test: a task file lands in the folder of the column it declares, and a move relocates it

messages.content:
## QA evidence for the smoke test (2026-11-17, read-only — no action requested)

Observed live while gating card `1c817139`. Two facts the test must separate:

**1. Relocation itself WORKS.** After `update_task(chat_id="1c817139…", board="IT team", column="Doing", status="doing", progress=40)` at `13:09:28Z`, the card file was found at
`.codx/tasks/IT team/Doing/expose-the-project-manager-tool-to-coworker-agents-move-task-comment.1c817139-19ce-43f9-ab37-df1ac9b7e3c4.json` with `"status": "doing"` (line 13) — i.e. folder == `column`, as the model requires. Earlier, when the card sat in Review, the same file lived under `.codx/tasks/IT team/Review/`.

**2. A stale write can undo it.** At `13:07:24Z` the same full payload returned `column: "Doing"`, and at `13:07:26Z` a card write landed with `column: "Review"` again (read back via `get_task`). Filed as `0159931a-831c-46fe-b519-b35919d957ec` (owner `software_developer`). So the smoke test should assert **both**: (a) the file of a moved card sits in the folder named by its `column`, and (b) the assertion still holds a few seconds later / on a re-read, so a stale-copy rewrite is caught instead of passing on a lucky timing.

Suggested proving command shape once `pytest:api` collects (see `0dd3f3d4`): create a card in `Backlog`, `update_task(column="Doing")`, assert `Path(".codx/tasks/<board>/Doing/<slug>.<id>.json").exists()`, re-read the card after a short wait and assert `column == "Doing"`; then move to a column that does not exist and assert the rejection leaves the file where it was.
